h1: The 7 Best Soundbars for Every Room and Budget in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 soundbars from Sonos, Bose, LG, Polk and Samsung, compared on Dolby Atmos, rear speakers, subwoofer, size and streaming.
summary: The Sonos Beam Gen 2 is the best soundbar for most homes, a compact Dolby Atmos bar that also joins the Sonos multi-room system. The Bose Smart Ultra is the premium pick with Alexa and Google voice, the LG S40TR is the only one here that includes true rear speakers, and the Samsung B400F is the budget bar with a built-in subwoofer.
intro: Soundbar shopping is a lesson in how little a number on the box tells you. A 2.0 bar, a 4.1 system and a 5.1.2 Atmos bar can sit at nearly the same price, and which one sounds best depends almost entirely on the room, the TV and how you listen. The honest starting question is not how many channels you want. It is whether you need the bar to sound big, sound clear or simply get out of the way.

We ranked seven soundbars across five brands, from a $50 to $100 Samsung with a built-in subwoofer to Bose's flagship Smart Ultra. They cover the main types: compact all-in-one bars, bars with a separate subwoofer, a system with rear speakers and Atmos models. We note the gaps in each listing, including missing power ratings.

products.name: Sonos Beam Gen 2, Black, Soundbar with Dolby Atmos
products.verdict: Genuine Dolby Atmos in a compact single unit, with access to the Sonos multi-room system.
products.description:
The Sonos Beam Gen 2 is a compact soundbar with Dolby Atmos support and full access to the Sonos multi-room ecosystem. It comes as a single unit and costs $200 to $500.

The Beam is the pick for most homes because it fits under almost any TV, supports Atmos formats and grows with your setup: you can add a Sonos subwoofer or rear speakers later, and use the bar with other Sonos speakers around the house. The multi-room ecosystem is the point for many buyers, since a bar becomes part of a whole-home music system. The compromise is that a bar this compact cannot match the bass or width of a bigger system without extra pieces.

Buy it for small to mid-size living rooms and for anyone who wants a system that can expand.
pros: Dolby Atmos in a compact bar
products.idealFor: Small to mid-size rooms and expandable setups.
products.skipIf: You want a bar with a bundled subwoofer.

products.name: Bose Smart Ultra Dolby Atmos Soundbar, HDMI eARC, Alexa and Google Voice
products.verdict: Premium Atmos sound with HDMI eARC and both Alexa and Google voice control.
products.description:
Bose's Smart Ultra is a premium Dolby Atmos soundbar with HDMI eARC and support for both Alexa and Google voice assistants. It costs $500 and up.

It ranks second because it is the most flexible voice-assistant bar here: you are not locked to one ecosystem. eARC carries lossless audio from the TV on one cable, and Atmos adds height. The price is the barrier, and it sits above what a small room needs.

Buy it for a main living room when sound quality and smart-home flexibility are both priorities. For small rooms, the Sonos Beam is better value.
pros: Alexa and Google voice both supported
products.idealFor: Main living rooms that need premium sound.
products.skipIf: Your room is small or your budget is tight.

products.name: LG S40TR 4.1 ch. Home Theater Soundbar with Rear Surround Speakers and
products.verdict: True rear surround speakers and a wireless subwoofer in the box, with AI Sound Pro.
products.description:
The LG S40TR is a 4.1 channel home theater soundbar that includes rear surround speakers and a wireless subwoofer, with AI Sound Pro processing. It costs $200 to $500.

It takes third place because real rear speakers do something no single bar can: put sound behind you, which makes movies and games feel wider. The wireless sub adds bass without cabling. No Atmos on the listing, so height effects are absent. Setup is more involved than with a single bar, since the rear speakers need power and placement.

Buy it for a movie room where you can place speakers behind the seats. Skip it if you want a one-box solution.
pros: Strong value for a full system
products.idealFor: Movie rooms where rear speakers can be placed.

products.name: Polk Audio Signa S2 Ultra-Slim Sound Bar for Smart TV with Subwoofer
products.verdict: A slim Polk bar with a bundled subwoofer for TVs with little clearance.
products.description:
The Polk Signa S2 is an ultra-slim soundbar for smart TVs that includes a subwoofer, from a long-established speaker brand. It costs $200 to $500.

Fourth place reflects a sound-first design for tight spaces. A slim profile slides beneath TVs with short stands, and Polk's loudspeaker background suggests a thoughtful tune. What you give up against the top picks is Atmos and modern streaming features, since the listing mentions neither.

Buy it if your TV sits low and you want bass in the box. Choose the Sonos if you want streaming features.
products.idealFor: TVs with little clearance beneath them.

products.name: Bose Smart Dolby Atmos Soundbar, All-in-One, Alexa Built-in, Black
products.verdict: Atmos, Alexa and AirPlay, Spotify Connect and Chromecast in one bar.
products.description:
This Bose all-in-one soundbar adds Dolby Atmos, built-in Alexa and streaming over AirPlay, Spotify Connect and Chromecast. It comes in black and costs $500 and up.

It lands fifth because it is expensive for what it does against the Sonos Beam, which also offers Atmos at a lower tier. Where Bose wins is in voice: Alexa is built in, and the streaming list is wide. If you prefer Bose's sound tuning, it is a good choice.

Buy it if you favour the Bose sound and already use Alexa. Otherwise save with the Sonos.
products.idealFor: Alexa homes that prefer Bose sound.
products.skipIf: You want the best value for Atmos.

products.name: Samsung B-Series Soundbar HW B400F 2.0ch with Built-In Subwoofer (2025)
products.verdict: A 2.0 channel bar with a built-in subwoofer and Voice Enhance, for $50 to $100.
products.description:
The Samsung HW-B400F is a 2.0 channel soundbar with a built-in subwoofer, a Voice Enhance mode and surround sound expansion. It costs $50 to $100 and is a 2025 model.

It places sixth because the bass is tied to a small driver inside the bar, so it cannot reach the depth of a separate sub, and 2.0 channels offer a narrow stage. For the price, it is a clear step up from TV speakers, and Voice Enhance makes speech easier to follow.

Buy it for a bedroom or a second TV. Skip it for a main movie room.

products.name: Bose TV Speaker, Soundbar for TV with Bluetooth and HDMI-ARC Connectivity
products.verdict: A compact all-in-one with HDMI-ARC, Bluetooth and a remote, at Bose's entry price.
products.description:
The Bose TV Speaker is a compact all-in-one soundbar with HDMI-ARC and Bluetooth connectivity and an included remote. It costs $200 to $500.

It finishes seventh because it focuses on clarity, not scale. It lacks Atmos and a subwoofer, and the price is the same as bars with more features. The strength is simplicity: plug in one cable and speech gets clearer.

Buy it if the main goal is hearing dialogue. Choose another bar for movies.
cons: Costs as much as bigger bars
products.idealFor: Anyone who mainly wants clearer speech.

methodology.title: System type
methodology.description: We compared single bars, bars with subwoofers, and a system with rear speakers by how much of a room they can fill.

methodology.title: Dolby Atmos and surround
methodology.description: Atmos support and true rear speakers were credited for immersion, while virtual surround claims counted for less.

methodology.title: Streaming and voice
methodology.description: Multi-room systems, Alexa, Google, AirPlay and Chromecast were weighed for how well each bar suits a connected home.

methodology.title: Size and fit
methodology.description: Compact and ultra-slim designs were rated for how easily they fit under real TVs and in small rooms.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Price tiers from $50 to $500 and up were compared with features, with expansion options counted as a plus.

whatMatters.detail: Atmos adds height by using upward-firing drivers or processing. It makes weather and aircraft sound overhead. It only matters if you watch Atmos content, which streaming and discs increasingly provide.
A subwoofer reproduces low frequencies that a slim bar cannot, and rear speakers add true surround. Separate pieces sound better but need space and outlets. Built-in subs save room but are weaker.
HDMI ARC or eARC is the cleanest connection, carrying audio back from the TV on one cable. eARC supports higher-quality formats. Check your TV's ports before buying.
Some bars join a multi-room system such as Sonos, and others support AirPlay, Spotify Connect or Chromecast. Pick the ecosystem you already use. An expandable system lets you add speakers over time.
A bar must fit between the TV's feet or on a stand, and not block the remote sensor. A slim bar suits a low TV. Measure the gap before ordering.

howToChoose.intro: Decide whether you want one box, a bar with a sub or a full surround system, and the field narrows fast.

cards.label: Atmos bar
cards.text: Uses upward-firing drivers for height in a single box. The Sonos Beam Gen 2 and both Bose Smart bars work this way.

cards.label: Rear-speaker system
cards.text: Real speakers behind the seating for wide surround. The LG S40TR includes them with a wireless subwoofer.

howToChoose.note: Choose an Atmos bar for simplicity, and a rear-speaker system if you have the room to place the extra pieces.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact bar, a modest subwoofer or none, and a low-volume or night mode. Choose placement that keeps bass off shared walls.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Sonos Beam Gen 2 is the best small-room bar, and the Samsung HW-B400F is the cheap option with a built-in sub.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a large room and watch films. The Bose Smart Ultra at $500 and up offers the biggest sound here.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The bar is for a bedroom or secondary TV. The Samsung B400F at $50 to $100 does the job.

faq.q: Do I need an eARC port?
faq.a: For the best Atmos quality, yes. ARC works for standard formats. Check your TV's HDMI labels before buying.

faq.q: What is the common mistake buying a soundbar?
faq.a: Buying by channel count and ignoring room size. A compact Atmos bar can sound better in a small room than a large system. Match the bar to the space.

faq.q: Is Sonos worth it over a cheaper bar?
faq.a: If you want multi-room music and the option to expand, yes. For a single-room TV upgrade, a cheaper bar may be enough.

faq.q: How do I set up a soundbar?
faq.a: Connect it to the TV's HDMI ARC port, plug in power and enable the TV's external speaker setting. Follow the app setup for Wi-Fi bars. Place rear speakers and subwoofer as the manual advises.

faq.q: Can I add a subwoofer later?
faq.a: Sonos and Bose both sell add-on subwoofers for some bars. Check compatibility before buying. Bars with built-in subs usually cannot be expanded.
Dust the grille with a soft brush and wipe the case with a dry cloth. Keep liquids away. Avoid sprays on fabric covers.

finalTake: The Sonos Beam Gen 2 is the best soundbar for most homes, thanks to its Atmos support and room to grow. The Bose Smart Ultra is the premium choice with both major voice assistants, and the LG S40TR is the pick if you want true rear speakers. For tight budgets, the Samsung B400F offers a built-in subwoofer for $50 to $100.
